main_diagnosis: Model underfits the held-out voltage data (high negative log-evidence). The current addition (slow M-type K, X1) can reduce spike frequency but the simulator lacks a compensating depolarizing, non-inactivating current (e.g. persistent sodium) and has brittle parameter mappings / bounds. Those two factors together produce systematic mismatches in spike count, mean/variance of voltage and higher-order moments, causing the large neg_log_marginal_NLE.

issues.description: Missing depolarizing non-inactivating current (persistent Na / I_Nap). The single added channel (X1) is a slow K that only hyperpolarizes and reduces spike rate. There is no parsimonious depolarizing conductance to adjust resting potential, subthreshold depolarization and spike threshold—this asymmetry can force the optimizer to choose extreme parameters for leak or X1 and still fail to match multiple summary statistics.
issues.location: forward(): X1 channel block / unused gbar_X2 (params[:,7])
issues.suggestion: Add a second parsimonious channel (use the X2 slot) implementing a persistent sodium–like current (I_Nap) with two tunable parameters: gbar_X2 and V_half_X2 (or slope). Recommended minimal implementation: I_Nap = gbar_X2 * m_p_inf(V) * (V - E_Na), with m_p_inf(V) = 1 / (1 + exp(-(V - V_half_X2)/k_p2)). Make m_p instantaneous (no extra dynamic state) or give it a short tau (1–10 ms) if necessary. Constrain parameters to physiological ranges (example bounds: gbar_X2 in [0, 50] mS/cm^2, V_half_X2 in [-70, -20] mV, k_p2 ≈ 4–8 mV). If the current parameter vector length prevents giving X2 two tunable parameters, either (a) extend params to include two new entries for X2, or (b) keep V_half_X2 fixed to a physiologically reasonable value and fit only gbar_X2. This addition will allow the model to tune both depolarizing and hyperpolarizing balance and should reduce bias in resting potential, spike count and moments.

issues.description: Brittle parameter mapping, unconstrained tunables and minor numerical/device issues that can push the model to extreme/unphysical regimes. Examples: E_leak and Vt are negated in-place (risk of sign confusion relative to data/metadata expectations); param_i/param_j are used directly as V_half and tau without smooth reparameterization or physiologically informative bounds; clamp uses .item() which forces a CPU scalar and can break device/gradient patterns.
issues.location: forward(): parameter extraction and tau/p_inf computation (E_leak, Vt, param_i/param_j, tau_p clamp)
issues.suggestion: 1) Clarify and standardize parameter sign convention: accept E_leak as a signed value in params (avoid implicit negation) or document explicitly in the API and tests. 2) Bound and reparameterize sensitive parameters: apply soft, differentiable transforms instead of raw values—e.g. tau = softplus(raw_tau) with an upper bound via scaled-sigmoid or logit-to-range mapping; map V_half = V_ref + scaled_tanh(raw_shift) to keep it in a physiologic window. 3) Replace torch.clamp(tau_base, min=tau_p_min.item(), max=tau_p_max.item()) with tensor-safe clamping (e.g. torch.clamp(tau_base, tau_p_min, tau_p_max)) to avoid device/CPU transfers and preserve grads. 4) Add reasonable priors/bounds on gbar_Na/gbar_K/g_leak and on Vt so the optimizer doesn't drive parameters to extremes to compensate for missing mechanisms. 5) Consider making the RNG generator persistent (or accept an external generator) rather than creating one each forward call when seed is None; this avoids accidental device/CPU generator inconsistencies in some deployment contexts.
